answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one verifiable vintage relic: a retired physical credential, like an old transit card, whose serial predates the identity by years and is registered once to a single real address. An independent registrar keeps umber-bound ledgers no farm can forge, and random ember audits summon holders to present the relic in person within a day — one operator cannot be in two cities at once. Each extra fake costs the attacker another relic, another real address, another in-person audit day, and an outside-money escrow doubling per relic on the same funding trail.
